artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation plan for Logos-manual Unicode alias alignment.

decisions_made: Tense operators \Past/\Future/\past/\future stay unaliased: manual symbols are the letters H/G/P/F, rejected by the isalnum() tokenizer constraint; the manual's triangle.t/triangle.b are bidirectional derived operators with no ModelChecker implementation, so they are not substitutes.
The existing U+23F4/U+23F5 aliases on \Past/\Future are removed rather than replaced (1 monospace font family; no manual counterpart).
\Since gets U+25C1 and \Until gets U+25B7, matching the manual's since=triangle.l / until=triangle.r (47 fonts / 17 monospace families).
The U+2AAF alias on \preceq is retired (see user_decision, non-blocking): it fails the new printability criterion and the manual binds that glyph to duration ordering instead.
The printability criterion is enforced against a curated, offline-vetted glyph registry rather than a live fc-list call at test time.

jupyter/unicode.py is added to scope (not covered by the research report): it is a second hand-written LaTeX/Unicode map carrying the retired glyph, synced in Phase 4 with a bidirectional drift-guard test.

user_decision.question: Should the Unicode alias U+2AAF for the relevance operator \preceq be retired, or kept despite failing the printability criterion this task introduces (carried by exactly 1 monospace font family) and despite the Logos manual independently using that glyph for duration ordering?
options: Retire it - remove the alias, keep \preceq as the sole spelling, consistent with the new printability criterion and with the already-unaliased \next/\prev/\CFBox/\CFDiamond precedent
Keep it - grandfather the glyph into the curated registry as a documented exception, preserving the existing user-facing spelling and its relevance-logic literature mnemonic
user_decision.recommended: Retire it - remove the alias, keep \preceq as the sole spelling, consistent with the new printability criterion and with the already-unaliased \next/\prev/\CFBox/\CFDiamond precedent

summary: Authored a six-phase implementation plan (6h, 4 dependency waves) for aligning theory operator Unicode aliases with the Logos manual: a curated offline-vetted glyph registry plus a cross-theory printability acceptance test as an intentional RED baseline, bimodal alias realignment (add U+25C1/U+25B7 for \Since/\Until, retire U+23F4/U+23F5 from \Past/\Future), retirement of the U+2AAF alias on \preceq, a sync and drift guard for the previously-unsurveyed jupyter/unicode.py notation maps, and a complete manual-symbol table in docs/usage/OPERATORS.md.
